name: A Farmer's Rice Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: a quart of rich milk or cream and milk mixed
ingredients.originalText: a quart of rich milk or cream and milk mixed
ingredients.quantityText: a quart of rich milk or cream and milk mixed

ingredients.name: quarter of a pound of brown sugar
ingredients.originalText: a quarter of a pound of brown sugar

instructions.text: Wash a common-sized tea-cup of rice through cold water.
Stir it raw into a quart of rich milk, or of cream and milk mixed; adding a quarter of a pound of brown sugar, and a table-spoonful of powdered cinnamon.
Put it into a deep pan, and bake it two hours or more.
When done, the rice will be perfectly soft, which you may ascertain by dipping a tea-spoon into the edge of the pudding and taking out a little to try.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Wash a common-sized tea-cup of rice through cold water.
2. Stir it raw into a quart of rich milk, or of cream and milk mixed; adding a quarter of a pound of brown sugar, and a table-spoonful of powdered cinnamon.
3. Put it into a deep pan, and bake it two hours or more.
4. When done, the rice will be perfectly soft, which you may ascertain by dipping a tea-spoon into the edge of the pudding and taking out a little to try.
5. Eat it cold.
